Return to the Stars

With his back against the proverbial wall, your commander ordered a somewhat daring raid on a Shwabolian outpost to break out of the strategic stalemate. Naturally, things didn't quite go as planned. Several members of your platoon were killed, and you were separated, captured, sedated, and taken to this prison... somewhere.
 
Initially, you settled into a sort of routine: sleep, shower, eat, reconsider your life choices, the occasional questioning impeded by language barriers, and back to sleep again. But it has been three days since your captors last fed you – or given you any attention, really. If you are to leave this planet alive, you better find a way before you starve...

Return to the Stars
An Interactive Escape by Adrian Welcker (ADRIFT 5 Edition)
Release 1 / Serial number 260718 / ADRIFT 5.0.0.36.6
Content Warning: descriptions of gore and violence.


Your Cell
This is the room you have spent most of your time in, ever since being taken captive. To be honest, you've kind of lost track of how long that has been.  A cot stands in one corner of the room.  A metal door lies to the north, keeping you securely in the cell.  A small camera hangs above the cot, keeping a watchful eye on you.  A sanitary station – a sort of hybrid toilet-shower-sink – is built into a corner of the room.  

> inventory
You are wearing a set of fatigues and a pair of black leather combat boots, and are carrying nothing.

> kick door
That was among the first things you tried when you got here. You've given up trying by now.

> look through door
You peek through the small, scuffed up duraplast window into the corridor outside. It is empty.

> listen
It has been eerily quiet for a few days now. Gone are the footsteps, the occasional shouting, the idle chit-chat of the guards. Now you hear nothing but the faint noise of the ventilation system.

> break camera
Needless violence won't get you off this rock any faster.

> pull grate
With a groan of exertion, you pull the grate with enough force for the old welds to give way. You set the grate down on the ground.

> crawl through duct
(first getting into the cell air duct)
You get into the air duct.  You crawl though the piping, air rushing past your face.


Prison Installations Room
You are lying in the in the bottom of the air duct, peeking out into the room:This is where most of the installations and appliances keeping the cell complex running reside.   A stiff breeze blows through this room, from the large machine on one wall, to the air ducts on the opposite wall.  

A ladder leads up.  On one of the walls is a panel with a number of large switches on it.

> kick grate
You kick the old grate, making a hole large enough for a person to squeeze through.

> out
(out of the bottom air duct)
You get out of the bottom air duct.

> x panel
A number of large rotary switches are attached to this panel. One is labeled "YVTUGF", the next "ZNTYBPX", a third "ZNTYBPX", and one is labeled "PBAGEBYF".

> up
You move up.

Prison Control Room
The walls are plastered with screens showing video feeds from throughout the facility. This must be the place from which the prisoners are monitored.

A ladder leads down into the installations room, and a corridor leads south.
A control desk and some screens are installed on the wall.  Your helmet is sitting on a table in the middle of the room, with a number of wires attached to it.

Shore Docks
The shoreline here seems more like an extension of the ocean floor you just walked: a gradual incline, rather than a sharp drop. A dock extends into the water to allow loading and unloading boats without needing to drive them up against the shore. (Although no boats are to be seen.)
You vaguely recall coming through here, weeks ago, sedated, a breathing mask strapped to your face...

The prison buildings lie to the south, down the muddy incline and across the water, and the military complex continues to the north.

> n
You move north.

There are several places you could go from here. The shoreline and the docks lie to the south. What looks like a hangar lies to the east, blocked off by a force field. A smaller building,  labeled "Barracks",  lies to the west, and a larger building with a sign reading "Command Center"  , blocked off by a door, lies to the north.  

The wind picks up some leaves and blows them through the force field to the east.[*]

Communal Washroom
This would be the place where the garrison force (if one can call it that, given the size of the facility) takes care of personal hygiene. It is a sterile-looking room, white tiles covering the floor and the walls all the way up to the ceiling. Four sinks and mirrors are installed on one wall, four toilets on another, the remaining two have two showers each. It doesn't seem like the Shwabolians care a whole lot about privacy, seeing as there are no dividers of any kind in the room.

The only way out is north, back to the barracks.

> shower
You turn on one of the showers and let the water run over you. The mud slides off your gear and collects on the floor before finding its way down the drain.

> cut larger alien's corpse with knife
You double-check inside the creature's mouth, but no dice. With a sigh, you kneel down in the puddle of blood now surrounding the body. You carefully position the makeshift knife, plunging it deep into the dead creature's abdominal area; guts, blood, and other bodily fluids spilling out and onto your armored legs as you cut.
With the incision complete, you take a second to steel yourself before reaching into the abdominal cavity. After a minute or so of fishing around in the bloody soup, you find the object of your desire: a small data crypt, which the creature swallowed when you came into the room. It appears to be undamaged.

You feel like throwing up.

> x larger corpse
A well and truly dead Shwabolian. Its lizard appendages lie splayed out in all directions. He is looking a bit worse for wear after you extracted the data crypt from inside him.

Landing Strip
You are standing on the tarmac of a small landing pad. It's not large enough for a fixed-wing atmospheric craft to take off, but perfectly adequate for the vertical take-off and landing operation of a space-capable vessel.

You could go south, through the launch doors and back into the hangar.

> enter ship
You step inside the messenger ship.  

Hangar (in the messenger ship)
You are sitting in the cockpit of the messenger ship. The control panels are dark and blank.

> put data crypt in notch
You place the data crypt into the notch on the control panel. It fits perfectly.

The ship beeps quietly.

> start ship
Luckily, Earth scientists were able to get their hands on a similar model of Shwabolian ship, so your suit is able to guide you through most of the pre-flight checks.

You press the button that your suit indicates as being the main switch for the ship. One by one, the messenger ship's systems come alive around you. The ship is now ready for launch.

> look through dome
The ship is standing on the landing pad outside the hangar.  The ship is floating in space, several hundred kilometers above the planet's sickly yellowish surface.

> launch
Launch what?

> look outside
Sorry, I'm not sure which object you are trying to launch.

> transition home
Yes, that's the plan.[*]

> launch ship
You get into the pilot's seat and take a few seconds to collect your thoughts. While you didn't perform absolutely terribly on the simulator tryouts in bootcamp, there is certainly a reason why you were placed with the space-borne infantry rather than in a dropship wing.[line break]
... no time for second thoughts. It's either this, or staying on this planet until you either starve or your captors return and discover what you did. After all, you (hopefully) won't need to fly any combat maneuvers, just take off and make orbit. You push your doubts aside and follow the pointers provided by you armor's computer system.

Half an hour later, you have safely left the atmosphere and have settled into a stable low orbit.

> look through dome
The ship is floating in space, several hundred kilometers above the planet's sickly yellowish surface.

> x transit node
A yellow dot on the ship's map marks the spot at which you can transition to Earth – it is not actually visible out there.

> transition home
While your sudden appearance in the solar system caused some confusion and concern, the transmission of your identification codes – and showing your face on video comms – dissuaded the combined military forces in the area from blowing you to pieces. Against your own expectations, you manage to land the ship in the hangar of one of the fleet's large carriers. You finally get something proper to eat and a fresh set of fatigues, then settle in for what promises to be about three lifetimes' worth of debriefings...

*** You have won ***
